title: Conquests of Alexander the Great
summary: In 334 BCE Alexander III of Macedon crossed into Asia and began his conquest of the Achaemenid Persian Empire, winning at the Granicus, Issus and Gaugamela. He took Egypt, Babylon and Susa and campaigned as far as the Punjab and the Indus valley. He made Babylon his capital and died there in 323 BCE. His generals then fought for supremacy, in the era known as the Hellenistic period.

uncertainty.note: Alexander crossed into Asia in the spring of 334 BCE (-333) and died in Babylon in June 323 BCE (-322).

as_recorded.value: crossed over to Asia Minor in 334 BCE to begin his conquest of the Achaemenid Persian Empire

importance.justification: Ended the Achaemenid Persian Empire and opened the Hellenistic period.
